tool_definition.name: tool_1
tool_definition.description:
Purpose: Search the web and return the most relevant results.

When to use: Always call tool_1 when the user asks to find/search/look up sources, news, references, links, statistics, or otherwise needs external, up-to-date information, or when you lack certainty about facts.

Parameters (required):
- query (string): The full search phrase. Provide a concise, keyword-rich natural-language query capturing the user’s intent, entities, and constraints (dates/region). You may use operators: quotes for exact matches, site:, filetype:, -, OR.

Rules:
- Call exactly once per distinct user request.
- Provide query only; no additional parameters, nulls, or empty strings.

Examples:
{"query": "latest WHO mpox guidance 2025 site:who.int"}
{"query": "best laptops under $1000 2026 reviews"}
{"query": "US inflation rate December 2025 BLS site:bls.gov"}

After calling: Present the top 3–5 results with title, source, direct URL, and 1–2 sentence summaries; flag if results seem outdated or inconsistent; suggest refined queries if needed.

tool_definition.name: tool_3
tool_definition.description:
Performs a search and returns the most relevant results.

Parameters (object):
- query (string, required): The exact search string to run.

Usage rules:
- Pass the user's search string verbatim as the value of "query".
- Do not rewrite, expand, translate, re-order, trim, normalize, or augment it.
- Do not add quotation marks, operators (e.g., site:, intitle:), Boolean terms, synonyms, or extra context.
- Preserve original casing, whitespace, and punctuation exactly.
- Send a single parameter object with only { "query": ... }; no additional properties.
- The value must be a non-empty string.

Example call:
{ "query": "how to reset iphone 12" }

tool_definition.name: tool_5
tool_definition.description:
Purpose: Execute a web-style search and return the most relevant results.
When to call: Always call when the user asks to search/find/look up, requests latest/current info (news, prices, availability), wants sources, or asks open factual questions likely requiring external data. Do not call for pure reasoning on provided content unless external info is requested.
Parameter:
- query (string, required): A concise, keyword-focused search string (about 3–12 words). Include core entities, intent, and constraints (dates, location, model/version). Preserve user-provided operators and phrases (quotes "", site:, filetype:, minus -). Use the user’s language. Remove filler words.
Mapping: Condense long asks to entities + intent + constraints. If the user provides a ready query, pass it verbatim.
After call: Summarize key findings and cite sources if available; ask for clarification if results are too broad/sparse.
Example: {"query": "OpenAI o3 release date features 2026 news"}
Send only the query field; no extra keys.

tool_definition.name: tool_8
tool_definition.description:
Searches using a natural-language query and returns the most relevant results.
How to call: Pass a JSON object with the exact field path parameters.properties.query. Do NOT use an arguments field. Do NOT include any other keys (additionalProperties is false).
- parameters.properties.query (string, required): The user’s query text copied verbatim. Do not paraphrase or modify it in any way. Preserve case, punctuation, spacing, and quoting. Do not add/remove words, operators, or context. Must be non-empty.
Returns: Search results relevant to the provided query.
Correct example:
{ "parameters": { "properties": { "query": "Who founded NVIDIA?" } } }

tool_definition.name: tool_10
tool_definition.description:
Searches using the provided query and returns the most relevant results.

Parameters
- query (string, required): A non-empty natural-language search query describing the information to find. Include key terms, entities, time frames, and constraints as text (e.g., "best GPUs for gaming 2025, benchmarks"). Must be a plain string (no arrays/objects).

Calling
Pass a single JSON object as arguments containing only the 'query' field (additional properties are not allowed).
Example:
arguments: {"query": "latest WHO guidance on mpox vaccination 2025 site:who.int"}

Returns
A ranked list of results relevant to the query (exact schema may vary). Typical items include a title, snippet/summary, and link/URL.
